seo_title: A Flower Virus Helped Trigger Europe’s First Recorded Asset Bubble
fact_hook: A plant virus helped inflate a national financial frenzy.

During Tulip Mania, infected bulbs became luxury status symbols commanding enormous prices. Investors did not understand the biological cause, attributing uniqueness to mystical rarity. When the speculative bubble burst, the same infected bulbs lost most of their value. A microscopic pathogen had inadvertently shaped one of history’s most famous financial manias.

The more biologically compromised the tulip, the more economically prized it became. This inversion of health and value underscores how perception can overpower material fundamentals. The Dutch Republic, famed for rational trade and accounting precision, suddenly faced ridicule across Europe.
impact_paragraph_2: Tulip Mania became a lasting symbol of speculative excess, invoked centuries later during stock bubbles and cryptocurrency surges.
